Subject: Regional data custody: scope & rollback protocol for NordicBank pilot

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time on Thursday. Following up with a focused ask to scope the pilot for Private (VPC) deployment. Attached is our initial scope doc (data-residency-scope-v1.pdf). High-level asks for confirmation so we can produce a runbook and rollback protocol: 

- Primary requirement: customer data (production tokens, user PII) must remain in EU jurisdictions for primary processing and long-term storage.
- Warm standby in APAC is allowed only for DR, subject to: encrypted in-transit, dual-authority KMS (customer-managed KMS in EU with key wrapping in APAC), and explicit auditor evidence for any cross-border telemetry.
- Non-production (staging/test) may be hosted in APAC if data is synthetic or explicitly masked.
- We need to confirm required evidence items for your audit team (logs, control-plane access records, KMS attestations, network egress lists).

Can you confirm the above and provide: procurement contact for a PO (if we need a reserved private pilot), and technical lead for KMS/networking?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the checklist items we should produce by 10/10.
2) We deliver a runbook + rollback protocol and a network IP/ASN list.
3) Schedule a 60-min technical walk on 10/14 (EU morning).

Thanks — leaning on Karhtik and Marissa to draft the topology and rollback flows once we have your constraints.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi —

Appreciate the clear framing. Confirming at a high level:

- EU-only for primary production pockets (all customer PII and transaction tokens).
- APAC may host a warm standby that can serve tokens only after key unwrapping by EU KMS authority. We require proof of KMS separation and a replayable audit trail for any rekeying or cross-region decrypts.
- No persistent backups of EU production data are to be stored in APAC. Temporary caches for failover allowed if encrypted and auto-evicted within the RTO window.

Procurement point: procurement@nordicbank.no (cc’d) — they will open a PO if we sign off on scope and SLA. Technical lead for KMS/networking: Kaito Sato (kaito.sato@astracloud.jp) — he is vendor lead for cloud connectivity in APAC and will coordinate on peering/IP ranges.

For auditors we need:
- Control-plane access logs (timestamped, signed) for any region changes.
- KMS key rotation history and key-wrapping proofs.
- Network egress IP list and BGP peering snapshots for acceptance testing.
- Runbook with explicit failover + rollback steps and a dry-run schedule.

Attached is our residency checklist (NB-residency-checklist.xlsx) — it maps to our internal evidence categories. Proposed meeting windows: 10/14 09:00–11:00 CET or 10/15 14:00–16:00 CET.

Regards,
Lena Olsen
Head of Cloud Compliance
NordicBank ASA

Date: 2025-10-05T15:20:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Regional data custody: scope & rollback protocol for NordicBank pilot

Thanks, Lena — that is very helpful. A few clarifications and proposed mitigations: 

1) KMS model: we will support customer-managed keys (CMK) in the EU region. APAC standby will only be able to access wrapped tokens; unwrap operations require an HSM-backed approval tied to EU KMS (dual-authority). We will produce a key-wrapping proof artifact and a replayable rotation log for auditors.

2) Network & peering: karthik will produce a minimal IP/ASN list and BGP peering snapshot for acceptance testing. We will also provide a signed manifest of egress IPs for the dry-run.

3) Backup policy: no scheduled snapshots will be replicated to APAC. Warm standby will use ephemeral caches with TTL aligned to your RTO; these are auto-evicted and scrubbed on failback.

4) Rollback protocol (summary):
   - Failover to APAC warm-standby (manual trigger) — limited to read-only token redemption with key-unwrapping approval required.
   - Verification window (10–15 minutes): audit trail verification and smoke tests.
   - If data integrity checks fail: immediate rollback to EU; we will maintain an immutable snapshot in EU for last-known-good state.

Action items:
- Karhtik: network IP/ASN list + BGP config for dry-run (due 2025-10-09).
- Marissa: runbook draft + rollback checklist (due 2025-10-10).
- Rishi: produce audit artifact template and sign-off checklist.

I’ve attached a first-pass network diagram (network-topology-draft.vsdx). Please flag anything missing. We can lock the 10/14 09:00 CET slot if that works for you.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-10-06T14:07:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Regional data custody: scope & rollback protocol for NordicBank pilot

Looping in with technical notes and a proposed dry-run plan. Quick bullets from the infra side: 

- Egress/Peering: we will provide a signed IP manifest and ASN list. For the dry-run we recommend establishing BGP sessions with a /28 advertised from Redwood to the customer edge (test-only).
- NAT & LB: keep NAT for control-plane only; token redemption passes through a private LB with source IP preservation for audit logs.
- KMS: EU HSM cluster exposes CMK via an internal API; unwrapping requests from APAC require an HSM attestation and an explicit approval token (we'll produce the approval workflow artifact).
- RTO/RPO: target RTO 15m for token redemption, RPO <= 0 (no data loss for EU primary) — warm standby will intentionally be read-only until manual unlock.
- Rollback steps (technical):
   1) Revoke APAC unwrapping tokens.
   2) Drain APAC caches and force re-auth against EU control-plane.
   3) Verify checksums against EU immutable snapshot.

Dry-run proposal: 2025-10-20 08:00–10:00 CET — we will perform a controlled failover, exercise approval workflow, collect logs (control-plane, KMS, network snapshots), and run the rollback sequence. Deliverables post-run: signed artifacts for auditors and a runbook update.

I’ll prepare the IP manifest and a BGP config sample by EOD 2025-10-09.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
